lead: Atlanta's heavy storms, big trees and red clay make water damage a year-round risk. DryBeacon helps homes and businesses from Buckhead to East Atlanta dry out fast.
risk: flash flooding along creeks, tree falls on roofs and wet crawl spaces
risk_short: flash floods, tree falls, crawl spaces
why: Atlanta's tree canopy is beautiful until a storm drops a limb through the roof. Severe storms and tropical remnants bring down trees across Buckhead, Virginia-Highland and Kirkwood. In September 2024, Helene's rain flooded Peachtree Creek and parts of Buckhead. In September 2009, days of rain flooded creeks across the metro.

Red clay soil drains slowly, so water pools against foundations and soaks crawl spaces, which are common in older homes. In 2024, major water main breaks downtown left much of the city under boil-water notices. Long, humid summers let mold grow fast after any leak.
image_alt: House with a damaged roof and window after a severe storm
image_caption: Falling trees during Atlanta storms often open roofs to heavy rain.
problems: Homes near Peachtree and Proctor creeks
tips: Have large trees near the house checked by an arborist.
Seal and dehumidify your crawl space.
Keep gutters clear; oak and pine debris clogs them fast.
Check city flood maps if you live near a creek.
areas: Calls come from Midtown, Buckhead, Virginia-Highland, Grant Park, West End, East Atlanta, Inman Park and Kirkwood, plus Decatur, Sandy Springs, Marietta, Roswell and Alpharetta.

faq.q: Who pays when a tree falls on my Atlanta house?
faq.a: Usually your homeowners policy, if the tree damaged the house, even if it came from a neighbor's yard. Water that gets in through the hole is generally part of the same claim. Tarp the opening quickly and keep receipts.
